 *KenPom spread is referenced in the article 
 Murray State vs. Hofstra
 Southaven, MS | 12:00 PM ET | ESPN+
 I'm a big fan of KenPom's 2-point distance stat. I think it does a really good job of signaling what type of quality looks you are getting inside the arc. Through three games, Hofstra is dead last nationally in that stat entering Monday night, shooting their twos 10 feet from the basket on average. For reference, that is 7.3 feet further than national leader Saint Louis. In their three D-I games, Hofstra has taken 42 rim attempts and 69 non-rim twos. That is not good.
 It's especially concerning given Murray State has allowed the 20th-fewest threes in the country. The Racers are pressuring far more than last year while still aiming to run teams off the 3-point line. If you combine the fact that Hofstra cannot get to the rim, will not get many 3-point opportunities, are second-last in free throw rate AND Murray State's 26th-ranked turnover defense, this seems like an utter disaster for Hofstra's offense.
 The Pride can really defend, and they are fine playing a softer coverage discouraging driving lanes for their opponents. Murray State's offense has lots of rim/3 components to it, so the Racers will have to be on the money from deep to score consistently here if they can't dominate in transition.
